research_subject: Frank v0.1 / self-hosted target CI continuity
problem_statement: Multiple accepted-target self-hosted workflows failed before Frank semantic tests during actions/checkout cleanup. Determine whether this is a semantic regression, concurrent runner/workfolder collision, or persistent runner-workspace contamination, then test the cheapest reversible mitigation.

observed_failure_chain.failure: EACCES unlink of runtime/claycode_eval_v1/__pycache__/analyzer.cpython-312.pyc in the persistent workspace
repository state no longer had a usable .git directory during checkout cleanup
observed_failure_chain.causal_interpretation: consistent with a prior partial cleanup leaving a malformed persistent checkout; not independently sufficient to prove the exact deletion sequence

hypotheses.claim: multiple active Runner.Listener instances sharing a work folder are mutating the same checkout
hypotheses.evidence: checkout-free canary observed exactly one Runner.Listener, exactly one Runner.Worker, and no shared resolved workFolder

hypotheses.claim: non-runner-owned artifacts in the persistent self-hosted workspace make checkout cleanup fail and poison following jobs
hypotheses.evidence: canary directly observed five root:root paths under runtime/claycode_eval_v1/__pycache__, including analyzer.cpython-312.pyc, the exact path named by the earlier EACCES failure; isolated per-run checkout then passed the same self.root gate content

hypotheses.claim: a particular current workflow or process can be identified as the producer of the root-owned cache
hypotheses.evidence: bounded current repository/workflow search did not establish a producer; do not infer one from the cache location alone

exact_one_go_oob.name: CHECKOUT_FREE_RUNNER_WORKSPACE_FORENSICS_CANARY
exact_one_go_oob.diagnostic_limitation: the explicit known-failing-path stat in the canary accidentally duplicated one Dr.-Unterweger path segment and printed absent; the independent bounded ownership walk still discovered the exact analyzer path and four sibling root-owned paths, so the ownership finding does not depend on the buggy stat

mitigation_replication.design: fetch exact candidate SHA into unique RUNNER_TEMP repository and execute all pre-existing self.root semantic and differential gates there
passed_checks: exact candidate fetch in isolated runner temp

parallel_worker_result.change: independently merged stronger self.root checkout isolation with RUNNER_TEMP, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and cleanup
parallel_worker_result.relationship_to_this_lane: independent same-direction implementation; supersedes duplicate merge need

swarm_coordination.duplicate_avoidance: PR #402 was closed after fresh-main refresh showed the stronger independently merged fix; no stale duplicate was forced onto main
swarm_coordination.unifieddb_lane: existing PR #392 and its successful specialized target workflow were observed and not duplicated

primary_source_basis.source: GitHub Docs - Self-hosted runners / ephemeral runners
primary_source_basis.used_for: runner isolation guidance and ephemeral-runner context
independent self-hosted EACCES precedent involving root-owned workspace files; discovery/support only, not sole evidence

negative_and_unknown_results: multiple-listener/shared-workfolder hypothesis was not supported by the checkout-free canary
GitHub actions/runners enumeration through the connected app returned 403, so no unsupported external runner-registration claim is made
a separate Deep Integrity portable job failure was not diagnosed and is not attributed to workspace contamination without evidence
pre-existing static-integrity failures remained in the differential audit, but candidate introduced zero new failures

architecture_delta.scope: accepted-target self-hosted CI continuity only; no Frank cognitive semantics change
architecture_delta.supported_change: critical self-hosted gates that must survive persistent workspace residue should use exact per-run isolated checkout state, preferably under RUNNER_TEMP, until the root-writing source is identified and eliminated
architecture_delta.continuity_requirement: persistent workspace ownership contamination becomes an explicit health/test obligation; checkout failure before semantic execution must be classified as infrastructure evidence, not semantic failure
architecture_delta.strongest_counterhypothesis: isolated checkout can mask but does not eliminate the unknown root writer; persistent runner directories may still accumulate contamination outside isolated job trees
architecture_delta.promotion_boundary: do not claim root cause fully closed until the producing process is identified or the persistent workspace is proven clean across repeated accepted-target jobs
architecture_delta.rollback: workflow-only isolation is reversible; no runtime state, model, training, authority, database, or Frank Harness semantics were changed

next_frontier: trace the root-owned claycode_eval_v1 cache producer using existing logs/provenance if available, without inventing attribution
coordinate any remaining critical self-hosted checkout migrations against fresh main to avoid duplicate edits
retain the checkout-free ownership canary or equivalent bounded health signal until contamination source is closed
continue FRANK_V0_1 semantic work only after infrastructure-vs-semantic failure classification is preserved
